extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of literary theory; general readers interested in Roland Barthes' methods
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Roland Barthes' method of reading a literary text by identifying and tracking five semiotic/narratological 'codes' (hermeneutic, proairetic, semantic, symbolic, cultural) and their interactions to produce plural interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermeneutic code (HER.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated with enigmas of the text: puzzles and mysteries that may or may not be answered; Barthes marks these instances 'HER.' (hermeneutic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barthes breaks the process of revealing truth via enigmas into a sequence (LXXXIX): Thematisation; Positioning; Formulation of the enigma; Promise of an answer; Fraud (circumvention of the true answer); Equivocation (mixture of fraud and truth); Blocking (the enigma cannot be solved); Suspended answer; Partial answer; Disclosure of the truth. Because it moves from question to answer, the hermeneutic code is 'irreversible'—once revealed, it cannot be unrevealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proairetic (action) code (ACT.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encompasses actions or small scene-like sequences that create narrative tension and drive the narrative forward; Barthes marks these 'ACT.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proairetic units are small anticipatory movements (example: saying someone 'had been sleeping' invites anticipation they will wake). These units assemble into a forward drive with spatial and temporal dimensions. The proairetic code is classed as 'irreversible' alongside the hermeneutic code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic (semic) code (SEM.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns meaning at the level of connotation in relation to character—the 'resonances' beyond literal denotation; Barthes marks this 'SEM.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantic signs construct evolving character through signifiers such as name, costume, physical appearance, psychological traits, speech, and lexis. These signifiers have unstable meanings that can develop themes across the story; track recurring signifiers and their shifting connotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic code (SYM.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produces structures of often paired symbolic meanings accumulated through the text to establish a larger interpretive framework; marked 'SYM.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic clusters often organize around oppositions (male/female, inside/outside, hidden/revealed, hot/cold). Barthes highlights key symbolic processes (in Sarrasine): rhetorical (antitheses), sexual (castration), and economic (origin of wealth). This structure is not stable—the 'writerly' reader follows these structures until they collapse, which is part of the text's pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural (referential) code (REF.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constituted by points where the text refers to common bodies of knowledge or axiomatic truths; marked 'REF.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes references to agreed external facts (example: the real-world Faubourg Saint-Honoré) and 'gnomic' assertions (general truths, e.g., 'all men daydream at parties'). Use the cultural code to connect textual elements to background knowledge, social beliefs, or received wisdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreversibility vs. reversibility of codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Barthes distinguishes two 'irreversible' codes (hermeneutic and proairetic) from three 'reversible' codes (semantic, symbolic, cultural).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irreversible codes involve moves that, once made (a secret revealed, an action completed), cannot be undone for the reader; reversible codes (SEM., SYM., REF.) can be invoked and reworked in multiple interpretive directions. When analyzing, note which codes fix meaning and which allow multivalent interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codes as 'voices' (voice mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Barthes assigns each code an associated voice that characterizes its interpretive stance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping in S/Z: proairetic → Voice of Empirics; semic/semantic → Voice of the Person; cultural → Voice of Science; hermeneutic → Voice of Truth; symbolic → Voice of Symbol. Use these voice associations to clarify how different kinds of commentary or interpretive energy operate in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality/multivalence of the text and the role of the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Barthes insists on the plurality of a text; codes should not be integrated into a single privileged interpretation—the reader is an active producer of meanings rather than a passive consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not seek to 'close' the text by forcing one overall structure; allow different readings to invoke and combine codes differently. Note Barthes' contrast between the 'classical' text (which enforces a model of integration) and the modern 'plural' text (which resists closure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural practice: mark and track occurrences of codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Barthes methodically moves through the text, denoting where and how each code functions—he marks occurrences (e.g., 'HER.', 'ACT.', 'SEM.', 'SYM.', 'REF.') and explains their usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, annotate the text with code labels when a unit exemplifies a code; compile systems or annexes (Barthes' Annexes) to outline how codes accumulate across the work. This systematic noting is essential to Barthes' analytic method.
